tasks.commitBody: The season editor's event list is gone, and the one thing it did that nothing else could do — turning a standalone event into a series — now lives on the event page, arriving in the same commit so there is no window where neither surface offers it. Delete needed no move: the event page already carries its own armed delete. Convert renders only on a standalone event, because converting a series child is meaningless and the agenda gives no clue which is which, and it fails closed while rights or season are unresolved — absent, not disabled, like every rights-gated control beside it. Its gate is deliberately different from its neighbour's: unassigning a series is a parent-value delete and owner-gated on the wire, but convert only creates a series and appends a parent, both editor-reachable, so it sits on the editor tier with a comment at the site explaining the split. The create-form hint that sent people to the season panel to convert is rewritten in all four locales to point at the event page. The relocated flow kept its entire behaviour contract — the tests moved their entry point and changed no assertion — and the one test that used the panel's event delete as a cheap reload trigger was re-pointed at series delete rather than deleted, because it is the only coverage of the panel staying open across a write-triggered reload. STATED CHOICES: <GREEN agent fills>.
